elaine: :rotating_light: audit alert — large-volume read activity from service account `analytics_read_sa` against prod.users and prod.events. Not normal for last 24h, ~1.2M rows returned in 58m. auditsvc posted the detector.

auditsvc: [alert] large_read_rate | actor=analytics_read_sa | src_ips=[34.88.12.4, 34.88.12.5] | rows_returned=1,200,432 | sample_query:\n````\nSELECT u.id, u.email, e.event_type, e.payload\nFROM prod.users u\nJOIN prod.events e ON e.user_id = u.id\nWHERE e.created_at >= '2026-03-19'\nORDER BY e.created_at DESC\nLIMIT 10000;\n````\n(we only logged the sample; full query text retention limited to 7d)

ashok: ack received. marking incident and starting containment steps. First ask: was this a scheduled analytics job or new rollout? @jamie any deploys that could explain increased join size?

jamie: no scheduled job for that SA. We did push a minor metrics change yesterday but it only touches staging. tagging :eyes:

sre-oncall: I applied a temporary query-rate limit on the analytics RBAC role (throttled reads to 10 qps) and added a network-level deny for src_ip 34.88.12.5. If that breaks dashboards we can rollback but containment first.

elaine: good. Also please revoke the service account key used for analytics_read_sa and rotate credentials. Command to revoke: `gcloud iam service-accounts keys delete <KEY_ID> --iam-account=analytics_read_sa@redwood-inference.iam.gserviceaccount.com`.

sec-bot: recommended checklist updated -> containment: rotate keys, restrict RBAC, capture full slow-query plan, export audit logs to long-term bucket, check KMS decrypt activity. :lock:

auditsvc: additional finding: 18 KMS decrypt attempts for `projects/rw-prod/locations/global/keyRings/customer/cryptoKeys/prod-db-key` associated with analytics_read_sa between 03:58-04:05 UTC. All succeeded. Logged principal: serviceAccount:analytics_read_sa@redwood-inference.iam.gserviceaccount.com

ashok: hmm — KMS decrypts by an analytics SA are unexpected. Could be that job requested encrypted PII columns. We need to determine if decrypted plaintext was exfiltrated. Steps: 1) preserve query and connection logs; 2) snapshot DB audit trail; 3) isolate the SA and revoke keys; 4) rotate KMS key if suspicion increases.

jamie: grabbing psql connection logs now. Query planner shows a nested loop + seq scan on users — terrible cardinality estimate. Might be a bug in the new analytics query generator that accidentally removed a filter, causing huge result sets. I will post plan snippet in a sec.

elaine: while jamie collects plans, @sre-oncall please create an immutable export of affected tables (users/events) for forensic teams and copy the DB WAL segments for the time window. Tag exports with incident id INC-2026-0319-01.

sre-oncall: done — export location: gs://rw-sec-forensics/INC-2026-0319-01/ and snapshot id snap-20260319-04. Also turned on verbose logging for DB connections for 72h.

jamie: plan snippet:\n````\nSeq Scan on users  (cost=0.00..12784.00 rows=1200000 width=256)\nNested Loop  (cost=0.00..980000.00 rows=1200000 width=512)\n-> Seq Scan on users u\n-> Index Scan using events_user_id_idx on events e  (cost=0.00..3.50 rows=1 width=128)\n````\nLooks like the WHERE clause that should have limited by org_id was missing.

elaine: root cause hypothesis: misplaced filter in analytics query generator -> unbounded join -> high-volume decrypts. Immediate remediation: patch generator to re-introduce org filter, add a pre-execution validator that rejects queries expected to return >100k rows for bulk-reads, and short-term: enforce RBAC to deny access to PII columns unless explicit approval.

ashok: agreed. Post-incident actions to add to playbook: 1) create a pre-exec estimator for estimated rows; 2) alert on KMS decrypt spikes >5 in 5m; 3) require KMS access be audited and require customer-key binding approvals; 4) tighten SA permissions to least-privilege.

elaine: I'll create the incident ticket and own the follow-ups. Drafting postmortem and notifying Legal/Compliance. Link to draft: https://docs.internal.redwood.inc/incident/INC-2026-0319-01 (will update). :memo:

jamie: pushed a hotfix to analytics-querygen to restore the org filter and added a unit test. Deploy id: deploy-20260319-aqg-7. Rolling to prod in canary now.

sre-oncall: monitoring shows read rate dropped to baseline after throttling and key revocation. KMS decrypts returned to normal levels. Will keep the throttle for 24h.

elaine: thanks team. Retrospective actions: update RBAC matrix, add long-term audit retention (30d -> 90d for query texts), add a regression test for query generator on production-like datasets. Closing immediate response; will track remediation in the postmortem.

sec-bot: incident status: contained -> monitoring. Assigned owners: elaine (postmortem), jamie (fix), ashok (RBAC/KMS review), sre-oncall (forensics + retention).
__notes: This document is a single Slack thread. Messages are short and use Slack conventions like @mentions, emoji, inline code and code blocks. Metadata fields are strings or list of strings as required.
